answer: A farm of 186 keys thus funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the anchor reward in the cedar ledger costs the operator directly, and the willow audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 37% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the hostile operator's own capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
